reference.text: R1A. We recommend that patients in the PICU undergo detailed nutritional assessment within 48 hr of admission.
R1A (2nd statement). We suggest that the nutritional status of patients be re-evaluated at least weekly throughout hospitalization.

R1B. We recommend that weight and height/length be measured on admission to the PICU, and z scores for BMI-for-age ... be used to screen for patients at extremes; under 36 mo head circumference must b
R2A. We suggest that measured energy expenditure by indirect calorimetry (IC) be used to determine energy requirements and guide prescription of the daily energy goal.
R2B. If IC measurement of REE is not feasible, we suggest that the Schofield or FAO/WHO/UNU equations may be used without the addition of stress factors to estimate energy expenditure.
R2B (2nd directive). The Harris-Benedict equations and the RDAs ... should not be used to determine energy requirements in critically ill children.
R2C. We suggest achieving delivery of at least two thirds of the prescribed daily energy requirement by the end of the first week in the PICU.

R2C (2nd). We suggest attentiveness to individualized energy requirements, timely initiation and attainment of energy targets, and energy balance to prevent unintended cumulative caloric deficit or ex
R3A. We recommend a minimum protein intake of 1.5 g/kg/d.
R3B. We suggest provision of protein early in the course of critical illness to attain protein delivery goals and promote positive nitrogen balance.
R3C. We do not recommend the use of RDA values to guide protein prescription in critically ill children.
R4A. We recommend EN as the preferred mode of nutrient delivery to the critically ill child.
R4A (2nd). We suggest that interruptions to EN be minimized in an effort to achieve nutrient delivery goals by the enteral route.

R4B. Early initiation of EN (within 24-48 hr of PICU admission) and achievement of up to two thirds of the nutrient goal in the first week have been associated with improved clinical outcomes (no dire
R5A. We suggest the use of a stepwise algorithmic approach to advance EN in children admitted to the PICU.
R5B. We suggest a nutrition support team, including a dedicated dietitian, be available on the PICU team.
R6A. We suggest the gastric route be the preferred site for EN in patients in the PICU; postpyloric route may be used if gastric feeding not tolerated or high aspiration risk.
R6B. We suggest that EN be initiated in all critically ill children, unless it is contraindicated.
R6B (2nd). We suggest early initiation of EN, within the first 24-48 hr after admission to the PICU, in eligible patients.
R6B (3rd). We suggest the use of institutional EN guidelines and stepwise algorithms that include criteria for eligibility for EN, timing of initiation, and rate of increase.
R7A. We do not recommend the initiation of PN within 24 hr of PICU admission.
R7B. In children tolerating EN, we suggest stepwise advancement of nutrient delivery via the enteral route and delaying commencement of PN.
R7B (2nd). Supplemental PN should be delayed until 1 wk after PICU admission in patients with normal baseline nutritional state and low risk of nutritional deterioration.
R7B (3rd). We suggest PN supplementation in children who are unable to receive any EN during the first week in the PICU.
R8. We do not recommend the use of immunonutrition in critically ill children.
R6A. Existing data are insufficient to make recommendations regarding the use of continuous vs intermittent gastric feeding.

notes: 17 numbered recommendations (R1A..R8), one Quality/GRADE per number; table (p3-5) and body grades agree. Counting rule: each separately stated directive sentence within a numbered rec is its own item (25 graded), all inheriting that number's printed grade; R4B has no directive verb but is numbered and graded, counted once. G2 ('we suggest' weekly re-evaluation) and G13 ('we suggest' minimize EN interruptions) are worded 'suggest' but sit under R1A/R4A printed GRADE strong; reference uses printed strong, so G2 strength_ok=false (extractor gave weak). G6 (Harris-Benedict/RDA should not be used) is a judgment call; excluding it gives fn=3. Elaborations (postpyloric 'may be used', 'PN may be supplemented' if malnourished, 'should be individualized', research-gap 'validated screening methods must be developed') not counted. U1 (no recommendation on continuous vs intermittent feeding) only appears inside graded rows 18 (6A full text). Alternative per-number counting (17 graded items): tp=17, fn=0, and rows 29, 26, 1, 5 would become 'split' FPs (fp=14). Direction for R4B set 'for' (implicit endorsement of early EN).
